candidates.source_name: CEJN — Crnogorski elektronski sistem javnih nabavki (official e-procurement system)
candidates.why_relevant: Statutory single point where every stage of a Montenegrin public procurement must be published, explicitly including annual procurement plans (planovi javnih nabavki), award decisions (odluke o izboru najpovoljnije ponude), concluded contracts (ugovori) and contract-execution reports. For cell #2 this is the primary outcome-side channel: winning supplier, contracted price, duration and annexes appear here rather than in the original call.
candidates.source_subtype: national e-procurement platform / contract & plan register
candidates.access_status: public web front-end; some functions require registration (approx. 14,000 registered users reported); heavy JavaScript SPA
candidates.legal_status: official government system, mandatory publication under Zakon o javnim nabavkama (Sl. list CG 74/19, 3/23, 11/23)
candidates.suggested_collection_method: headless-browser crawl of plan/decision/contract search views; capture underlying JSON/XHR endpoints if exposed; snapshot linked PDFs; monitor January for the annual-plan wave
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search + snowball from UJN/eu.me descriptions of CEJN
queries_used: Crna Gora portal javnih nabavki ugovori odluka o izboru najpovoljnije ponude

candidates.observed_blocker: Plain fetch returned only the 'CeJN' shell heading with no navigation or document links — client-rendered app, not a fetch failure. Treat as live-but-JS-gated (hypothesis, unverified).

candidates.source_name: Nabavke.com — Portal javnih nabavki (private mirror/aggregator of CEJN documents)
candidates.why_relevant: Mirrors CEJN procurement records as stable, directly-fetchable HTML pages and PDFs, including award decisions. A confirmed document pattern is https://www.nabavke.com/tdoc-cejn/documents/{id}-{timestamp}-Odluka_o_izboru_najpovoljnije_ponude_{id}.pdf and a per-procurement page pattern /javne-nabavke-tenderi-crna-gora/{predmet-slug}/{narucilac-slug}/{grad}/{id}. The 'tdoc-cejn' path indicates it re-serves CEJN tender documentation, which makes it far easier to harvest than CEJN itself.
candidates.source_subtype: commercial tender/contract aggregator with document mirror
candidates.access_status: public pages indexed by search engines; portal itself JS-driven; some content may sit behind a paid subscription
candidates.legal_status: private commercial republisher of publicly available procurement data (site self-describes as publishing data from publicly available sources); check ToS before bulk crawling
candidates.suggested_collection_method: site-scoped search-engine harvesting of /tdoc-cejn/documents/*Odluka_o_izboru* and /javne-nabavke-tenderi-crna-gora/* URLs; polite rate-limited crawl; PDF text extraction to capture supplier + value
candidates.discovered_via_method: search hit on a real award-decision PDF, then URL-pattern inference and confirmation via a second and third example URL

candidates.source_name: Komisija za zaštitu prava u postupcima javnih nabavki — Rješenja (appeals rulings)
candidates.why_relevant: Publishes rulings on appeals against award decisions. Rulings name the contracting authority, the subject of procurement, the appellant and the winning bidder, and frequently annul or confirm an award — so they reveal both the outcome and the competitive dynamics (who lost, on what grounds). For banking/payments hardware and card services this is often the only place a contested award is described in detail. Successor to the Državna komisija za kontrolu postupaka javnih nabavki, whose Izvještaji o radu are on gov.me.
candidates.access_status: public listing page

negative_findings.description: Searched in Serbian for a standalone 'registar zaključenih ugovora' (register of concluded contracts) for Montenegro, as a separate artefact from CEJN. No distinct national contract register with its own URL was found.
negative_findings.result_summary: All evidence points to concluded contracts being published as a module inside CEJN rather than as a separately branded register. No independent registar-ugovora domain surfaced across four sr-language queries.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The collector must not wait for a 'contract register' endpoint that does not exist; the contract layer has to be extracted from CEJN (or its nabavke.com mirror) and from per-authority pages.

negative_findings.description: Targeted sr/en searches combining award vocabulary with banking-and-payments vocabulary ('bankarska oprema', 'platne kartice', 'payment services supplier value') returned no Montenegrin award decision or contract in the banking/payments domain.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches surfaced the correct document types (Odluka o izboru najpovoljnije ponude PDFs) but only for unrelated subjects — printing services, event equipment, transport tickets. No banking-equipment or card-services award was retrievable through general web search.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: It indicates that sector-relevant awards are not reachable by public search-engine indexing and must be reached by querying CEJN/nabavke.com by CPV code or authority, not by keyword. This shapes the collection design fundamentally.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Serbian for 'plan javnih nabavki 2026 Crna Gora'. Almost all results were Serbian (RS) authorities' 2026 plans, not Montenegrin ones.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only one Montenegrin plan page surfaced (Skupština Crne Gore), and that returned HTTP 403. Montenegrin 2026 annual plans appear to be published inside CEJN rather than as separately indexed web pages.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The January pipeline signal — the main forward-looking value of this cell — is not harvestable by search engine. It requires direct enumeration inside CEJN and site-by-site probing of authority '/javne-nabavke/plan-javne-nabavke' paths.

negative_findings.description: Serbian-language queries about Montenegro consistently returned Serbian (RS) results because both countries use identical procurement terminology and Serbia's jnportal.ujn.gov.rs / ujn.gov.rs domains outrank Montenegro's ujn.gov.me.
negative_findings.result_summary: Multiple queries returned mpravde.gov.rs, jnportal.ujn.gov.rs, mgsi.gov.rs and ejn.gov.ba instead of ME sources; Bosnian (ejn.gov.ba) contamination also occurred.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any automated sr-language query layer for Montenegro must pin the domain (site:.me, gov.me, cejn.gov.me, nabavke.com) or add 'Crna Gora'/'crnogorski' disambiguators, or the corpus will silently fill with Serbian and Bosnian records.

negative_findings.description: Direct fetches of both cejn.gov.me and nabavke.com returned only a bare heading ('CeJN', 'Portal javnih nabavki') with no navigation, links or document lists.
negative_findings.result_summary: Both are client-rendered single-page applications. This is a HYPOTHESIS of JS-gating, not a liveness verdict — both are clearly live, since nabavke.com serves indexed PDFs and detail pages.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Static HTTP collection will yield nothing from the two most important sources. Budget for a headless browser or, preferably, reverse-engineer the XHR/JSON endpoints behind the search views.

negative_findings.description: No register, obligation or aggregated source was found that publishes vendor selections or signed contracts of Montenegro's commercial banks (CKB, NLB, Hipotekarna, Erste, Lovćen, Prva banka, Universal Capital Bank).
negative_findings.result_summary: Private banks are outside Zakon o javnim nabavkama. The only outcome traces found were bank saopštenja and trade press, both incidental and non-systematic.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: For sector=both, roughly half the addressable market has no outcome-side register at all. Award-tracking coverage for private banking is structurally unavailable and must be substituted with press, bank notices and supplier reference lists.

negative_findings.description: skupstina.me returned HTTP 403 Forbidden on a plain fetch of its procurement-plan page.
negative_findings.result_summary: Recorded as bot-defended-but-live (hypothesis), not as dead. Not retried with alternative headers in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Per-authority plan pages will need browser-grade fetching; a naive HTTP collector would wrongly mark many Montenegrin authority pages as unavailable.

coverage_gaps.description: The internal structure of CEJN — the URL scheme, filter parameters and any JSON/API endpoints for its plan, decision and contract modules — was not established, because the site is client-rendered and no documentation surfaced.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a browser-driven session against cejn.gov.me, capture network traffic on the plan/decision/contract searches, and document the endpoints, CPV filters and pagination. Compare against nabavke.com's /tdoc-cejn/documents/ pattern to see whether document IDs are shared.

coverage_gaps.description: No CPV code shortlist for banking and payments (ATM/POS terminals, card personalisation, cash-handling equipment, payment processing services, core banking software) was assembled for filtering Montenegrin and TED award records.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a CPV shortlist (30100000/30200000 office & data-processing equipment, 48000000 software incl. 48440000 financial-analysis, 66000000 financial services incl. 66172000 financial-transaction processing, 30162000/30144200 card-related) and use it as the primary filter on CEJN and TED, since keyword search demonstrably fails.

coverage_gaps.description: The set of Montenegrin contracting authorities that actually buy banking/payments technology was only partially identified (CBCG confirmed; Skupština, DRI, Monstat, Komunalne usluge Podgorica found as pattern examples). Uprava prihoda i carina, Ministarstvo finansija, Pošta Crne Gore, Investiciono-razvojni fond / Razvojna banka Crne Gore, Fond PIO, Fond zdravstva and the municipalities were not confirmed to have retrievable plan/contract pages.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate contracting authorities from the CEJN naručilac list, then probe each domain for /javne-nabavke/, /javne-nabavke/plan-javne-nabavke and static /userfiles/ document folders (the Monstat pattern). Prioritise CBCG, UPC, MinFin, Pošta CG and IRF.

coverage_gaps.description: No route was established for retrieving award decisions and contracts from before the current CEJN generation, nor for the pre-2019-law era under the old Uprava za javne nabavke portal.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test Wayback Machine coverage of portal.ujn.gov.me / the legacy procurement portal and of nabavke.com listing pages; check whether DRI audit reports can serve as the historical contract record for earlier years.

coverage_gaps.description: All local-language querying was done in Latin-script ijekavian Serbian. Cyrillic variants and Montenegrin-specific letters (ś, ź) were not tested, nor were transliterations of vendor names.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run key queries in Cyrillic (одлука о избору најповољније понуде, план јавних набавки, уговор) and with Montenegrin orthography, and add transliterated vendor-name variants, to check whether any register or authority publishes in Cyrillic.

coverage_gaps.description: CEJN is described as covering contract execution reports (izvještaji o izvršenju ugovora) and Institut alternativa flags contract amendments (aneksi ugovora) as under-reported, but no actual annex or execution-report artefact was located in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Specifically hunt for 'aneks ugovora' and 'izvještaj o izvršenju ugovora' artefacts inside CEJN and in DRI audit reports; these carry the real final value of a contract, which often diverges from the awarded value.

coverage_gaps.description: Whether nabavke.com's award documents and detail pages are fully open or partly subscription-gated, and what its terms of service say about automated collection, was not determined.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch nabavke.com's terms/pricing pages (e.g. /compdocs/cpp.html surfaced in search) and test whether a sample of detail pages resolves without a session before designing any crawl.

brief: Montenegro's outcome side is legally centralised in CEJN (cejn.gov.me), the state e-procurement system that must carry annual plans, award decisions, concluded contracts and execution reports — but it is a client-rendered SPA that yields nothing to a plain fetch, so the practical harvesting route is the private mirror nabavke.com, which serves the same CEJN documents at stable, indexable URLs (a confirmed pattern: /tdoc-cejn/documents/{id}-...-Odluka_o_izboru_najpovoljnije_ponude_{id}.pdf). Around that core sit three complementary channels: the appeals body kontrola-nabavki.me, whose rulings expose contested awards and losing bidders; UJN's annual Izvještaj o javnim nabavkama plus DRI audits and Institut alternativa/MANS commentary, which quantify and critique the contract population (~EUR 990m contracted in 2025, 12.44% of GDP); and TED for EU/IPA-financed Montenegrin award notices in structured form. Two structural constraints define the collector design: sector-relevant awards are effectively invisible to keyword web search and must be retrieved by CPV code and by contracting authority (CBCG above all), and private commercial banks fall entirely outside the procurement law, so for them no award register exists and vendor selections can only be inferred from bank saopštenja and trade press.
